title: Introduce elastic lane throttler and fairness smoothing for continuous-batcher
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context and motivation:
This PR implements a new admission layer for the continuous-batcher we call the 'elastic lane throttler'. The goal is to reduce starvation of small/latency-sensitive lanes while retaining batching efficiency for throughput-heavy lanes. The previous continuous-batcher showed occasional head-of-line and lane-starvation spikes when a small number of long-sequence requests monopolized slots; debugging traces pointed at aggressive slot grabs + KV-prefetch noise.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds lane-based admission tokens: each incoming request is assigned to a lane (latency, balanced, throughput) by heuristics in scheduler based on sequence length, model hint, and request metadata. Lanes have token buckets with adjustable refill rates to shape steady-state admission.
- Introduces "patience credits": every request accrues a tiny aging credit while queued; the scheduler uses the decaying-credit to break starvation by temporarily elevating aged requests across lanes. Credits decay exponentially after dispatch to avoid long-term priority inversion.
- KV cache warmup hint propagation: requests that touch warm KV keys now annotate the admission token so they can be coalesced or admitted preferentially when cache locality can reduce per-token cost.
- Soft-timeout + jittered backoff: instead of a single hard queue timeout that would force-drop or preempt, the scheduler now installs a soft-timeout that triggers a gentle admission boost for aged requests and a jittered backoff to avoid synchronized mass-promotions.
- Kernel-aware slot sizing: scheduler consults kernel selector with a small scoring API (seq_len_estimate + quantized_cost_hint) to pick more appropriate slot sizes when mixing short and long sequences in a batch. This reduces wasted kernel occupancy and tail latency for short lanes.

Files changed (summary):
- runtime/batcher/elastic_lane_throttler.go: new admission layer with lane definitions, token buckets, patience credits and soft-timeout logic.
- runtime/scheduler/score_advisor.go: small API to expose seq-length/cost hints from kernel selector to scheduler.
- runtime/kv/cache_manager.go: add warmup-hint annotation on requests and a helper to surface KV locality to scheduler.
- runtime/kernel_selector/score.rs: add a compact estimator used by the scheduler for slot-sizing.
- pkg/metrics/queue_metrics.go: new metrics for lane_fill, patience_credits, soft_timeouts_triggered, kv_locality_hits.
- runtime/batcher/elastic_lane_throttler_test.go: unit and integration tests covering fairness, starvation scenarios and warmup-hint flows.

Commits (high-level):
- a1f9d8c: initial implementation of elastic lane throttler + basic token buckets
- b2c3e4a: add patience credit model and soft-timeout/jitter behavior
- c8d7e12: wire KV warmup hints into scheduler path, metric plumbing
- d3f5b8f: kernel score advisor and slot-sizing tweaks
- e7a12b4: tests, benchmarks, and docs updates

Testing and results:
- Unit tests: deterministic tests for token refill and patience credit accrual (fast).
- Integration: a replay harness with mixed short/long traffic (90th/99th latency targets) shows 20-35% reduction in short-request tail latency under heavy long-request pressure, with <3% throughput regression on large sequences. KV locality-aware paths reduced per-token compute by ~6% for workloads with >30% warm-key reuse.
- Canary: gradual rollout on a single machine pool for 48h with active tracing and SLA gates. No regressions observed; a few edge-case races found and fixed (see review thread).

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag (default off).
2) Enable on canary pool (single region) for 48h.
3) Gradually increase to 10% of pools, monitor lane_fill, patience_credits, soft_timeouts_triggered, latency SLOs.
4) Full rollout if no regressions and after ops sign-off.

Backward compatibility and configuration:
- Feature gated (config flag continuous.batch.elastic_lane_throttler).
- All parameters (bucket refill rates, patience decay, soft-timeout values) exposed via runtime config and per-customer overrides for Dedicated/Private.

Notes on safety and risk:
- The algorithm is conservative: token buckets default to generous refill for latency lane and small refill for throughput lane to avoid harming short requests.
- Soft-timeout uses jittered promotions and is intended to avoid synchronized wake-ups; still possible to see transient metric spikes — dashboard alerts added.

Related Linear tickets: ENG-4129 (Continuous batch fairness), ENG-4151 (KV hint propagation).

Test plan: unit/integration/e2e described above, new benchmarks added to benchmark-lab.

review_comments: Samir Rao: Can the patience credits cause long-running requests to starve again if we mis-tune decay? Recommend a circuit-breaker cap on promotions (author: added cap and test).
Ellen Park: Found a race in token bucket refill during pool shutdown (author: added mutex + unit test; CI rerun passed).
Diego Morales: Kernel score advisor looks good; suggest logging when slot-sizing changes batch composition to aid debugs (author: added sparse log at debug level).
Ops (Helen Tsai): Add dashboard panels for patience credits and soft-timeouts; set alert if soft_timeouts_triggered > 100/min on a pool (author: added panels and alert rules).
release_notes: Introduce elastic lane throttler: lane-based admission + patience credits, KV locality hints, kernel-aware slot-sizing and soft-timeouts to reduce starvation and short-request tail latency. Feature gated; disabled by default.
